title: Use an annotated illustration to show what each part of a document tells a reader.
rule: Redraw the document in vector with its own words and nothing invented, mark each part with a numbered disc in the text’s ink, and list the parts beside it, or under it on a phone, in the order they sit on the page, each with its name in bold and what it tells a reader. Where the drawing stops partway down, crop it at an open edge and say so in a note. Draw a dash the page prints as a rule one em wide, and give the table each part with its words as printed.
use_when: The reader asks what the parts of one document mean, such as what the first page of a law tells them.

use_instead.when: The steps a bill or rule goes through
How an institution makes a decision

text: A reader learns a document’s parts fastest on the page itself, where each part sits, and the numbered list carries the names to a reader who cannot see the drawing. Redrawing with the page’s own words keeps every callout checkable against the source.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form annotated-illustration: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s93; encode key, part, text and tells; labels.layout sets each block of the page in order (slot head, main or margin), with breaks, a bold lead and the margin block beside its line.
